conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim is false and states that there is no evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion: the claim is false.** There is no reliable evidence that drinking water boiled with garlic cures COVID-19.

The strongest directly relevant source here is the World Health Organization: it says garlic may have some antimicrobial properties as a food, but **there is no evidence that eating garlic protects people from COVID-19**. A lack of evidence for prevention also does not support the much stronger claim that boiled garlic water can *cure* an established infection. WHO further states that there was no licensed medication that “cures” COVID-19 (as of its 2022 myth-buster guidance), and advises people with symptoms to contact a health provider or COVID-19 hotline.

Independent fact-check reporting specifically investigated the “freshly boiled garlic water” assertion and found it false: there was no cure for the virus. AFP likewise reported that health professionals said from early 2020 that there was no evidence for boiled garlic as an effective treatment.

Garlic can be part of a normal diet, but it should not replace medical assessment or proven treatment. For people at higher risk of severe illness, CDC identifies authorized/approved antiviral medicines; evidence supports prompt antiviral treatment in eligible patients to reduce hospitalization and death.
